desc: Derive/verify the counting argument: each unordered cell pair appears in exactly C(mn−2, k−2) arrangements; confirmed with both examples (factor 1 for 2×2,k=2; factor C(2,1)=2 for 1×4,k=3).
Derive helper line_sum(L) = L(L²−1)/6 = Σ_{i<j}(j−i) for a line of length L; verified L=2→1, L=4→10.
Derive total pair-distance sum: S = n²·line_sum(m) + m²·line_sum(n); verified S=8 (2×2) and S=10 (1×4).
Implement `distanceSum`: factorials/inverse factorials up to N=m·n, C(N−2, k−2), S via modular inverse of 6, return C·S mod p. Code matches derivation exactly.
Verify against examples and edge cases: 2×2,k=2 → 8 ✓; 1×4,k=3 → 20 ✓; 1×2,k=2 → 1 ✓; 1×3,k=3 → 4 ✓; m=1/n=1 terms vanish naturally; k=2 and k=mn handled; O(mn) ≤ 10^5 performance fine.
